name: Siwa Oasis
tagline: Remote desert oasis of salt lakes and mud-brick ruins
summary: Siwa is a remote oasis deep in Egypt's Western Desert near the Libyan border, home to a Berber-speaking community. Climb the melting mud-brick fortress of Shali, see the Temple of the Oracle that Alexander the Great consulted, float in turquoise salt pools, bathe in Cleopatra's Spring and ride over the Great Sand Sea dunes at sunset.
seasonNote: October to March; summer is extremely hot.
arrival: About 9 hours by bus or car from Cairo via Marsa Matruh (4 hours from Matruh); check travel permits.
gettingAround: Bicycles and donkey carts in town; 4x4 tours for the desert.
cashTip: Carry Egyptian pounds in small notes for taxis, tips and cafés; cards work in hotels. Tipping (baksheesh) is expected for small services.
foodTip: Dates, olives, Siwan flatbread and slow-cooked lamb under the sand.
buyTip: Siwan dates, olive oil and embroidered textiles.
